exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: My brother is hungry.
exercises.german: Mein Bruder hat Hunger.
exercises.why: haben plus an accusative noun expresses hunger without an infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: Are you in a hurry?
exercises.german: Hast du es eilig?
exercises.why: The predicative complement of the accented es is an adjective, not a verb.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: I do not have time today.
exercises.german: Ich habe heute keine Zeit.
exercises.why: A time noun in the accusative replaces the infinitive of the default modal pattern.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: The company has a heavy debt burden.
exercises.german: Die Firma hat eine große Schuldenlast.
exercises.why: haben plus an accusative noun of state, with no infinitive anywhere in the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: Do you feel like going to the cinema?
exercises.german: Hast du Lust, ins Kino zu gehen?
exercises.why: haben plus Lust is completed by a zu-infinitive clause of its own.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: She was afraid of making a mistake.
exercises.german: Sie hatte Angst, einen Fehler zu machen.
exercises.why: A past form of the haben pattern with a zu-infinitive clause after the noun.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: I have reason to complain about the noise.
exercises.german: Ich habe Grund, mich über den Lärm zu beschweren.
exercises.why: haben plus a noun, with a reflexive zu-infinitive clause as its complement.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: The child has no fear of dogs.
exercises.german: Das Kind hat keine Angst vor Hunden.
exercises.why: Angst is the accusative object; vor takes the dative.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: Do you have a lot of work to do?
exercises.german: Hast du viel Arbeit zu erledigen?
exercises.why: A zu-infinitive clause stands in the slot after the noun, not after the modal.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: We have a meeting at nine.
exercises.german: Wir haben eine Besprechung um neun.
exercises.why: A time adverbial closes a clause whose only verb is the haben of the modal pattern.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: I have an appointment at the doctor tomorrow.
exercises.german: Ich habe morgen einen Termin beim Arzt.
exercises.why: Two prepositional additions follow a plain accusative noun as the modal complement.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: He has a good eye for detail.
exercises.german: Er hat ein gutes Auge für Details.
exercises.why: haben plus a noun phrase, with für governing the accusative inside it.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: She has a clear opinion on the subject.
exercises.german: Sie hat eine klare Meinung zu dem Thema.
exercises.why: haben plus an accusative noun plus a prepositional phrase naming the domain.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: We have no choice but to leave.
exercises.german: Wir haben keine andere Wahl, als zu gehen.
exercises.why: The als-clause of the zu-infinitive complement is set off by a comma.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: How much time do I have?
exercises.german: Wie viel Zeit habe ich?
exercises.why: A question with the modal in position two and an accusative noun as complement.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: You have to see to that rule.
exercises.german: Du musst dich um diese Regel kümmern.
exercises.why: sich kümmern um takes the accusative, with the reflexive pronoun between modal and preposition.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: You have my word for it.
exercises.german: Du hast mein Wort dafür.
exercises.why: A noun phrase with a da-compound standing in for für das.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: I have no time to waste.
exercises.german: Ich habe keine Zeit zu verschwenden.
exercises.why: The zu-infinitive after the noun keeps the verb last in the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: Do you have a lighter?
exercises.german: Hast du ein Feuerzeug?
exercises.why: A short question showing the plain accusative noun complement of a modal haben.

exercises.skill: Modal + noun phrase instead of infinitive
exercises.english: He has the right to complain.
exercises.german: Er hat das Recht, sich zu beschweren.
exercises.why: haben plus a noun of entitlement with a reflexive zu-infinitive clause.

exercises.english: You have to answer for that mistake.
exercises.german: Du musst für diesen Fehler geradestehen.
exercises.why: geradestehen für governs the accusative, which the modal carries along.

exercises.english: We must insist on this condition.
exercises.german: Wir müssen auf diese Bedingung bestehen.
exercises.why: bestehen auf governs the accusative, and the modal keeps the second slot in the main clause.

exercises.english: We can achieve a lot without your help.
exercises.german: Wir können ohne deine Hilfe viel erreichen.
exercises.why: The ohne-phrase follows the modal directly and stands in front of the infinitive.

exercises.english: What is that supposed to be for?
exercises.german: Wofür soll das denn gut sein?
exercises.why: The da-compound für das is question word and complement in one.

exercises.english: We must rely on your judgement.
exercises.german: Wir müssen uns auf dein Urteil verlassen.
exercises.why: The reflexive dative pronoun sits between the modal and the preposition.

exercises.english: He is not allowed to talk to the press.
exercises.german: Er darf nicht mit der Presse sprechen.
exercises.why: Modal, negation and a mit-phrase, with the infinitive closing the clause.

exercises.english: Can you take responsibility for that?
exercises.german: Kannst du dafür die Verantwortung übernehmen?
exercises.why: A da-compound precedes the accusative object in the finite clause.

exercises.english: We must not blame the messenger.
exercises.german: Wir dürfen den Boten nicht für die Nachricht verantwortlich machen.
exercises.why: A long accusative object sits between the modal and its prepositional phrase.

exercises.english: I must make do with what I have.
exercises.german: Ich muss mich mit dem begnügen, was ich habe.
exercises.why: A modal with a reflexive pronoun and a mit-phrase, plus a second clause.

exercises.english: You should be aware of the risk.
exercises.german: Du solltest dich des Risikos bewusst sein.
exercises.why: bewusst sein takes a genitive object, which the modal makes possible.

exercises.english: We must stay away from the water.
exercises.german: Wir müssen vom Wasser wegbleiben.
exercises.why: A prepositional phrase with a verb of motion and no infinitive complement.

exercises.english: You should be ashamed of your behaviour.
exercises.german: Du solltest dich deines Verhaltens schämen.
exercises.why: sich schämen takes a genitive; the reflexive pronoun is dative here.

exercises.english: We can count on him.
exercises.german: Auf ihn können wir uns verlassen.
exercises.why: The prepositional phrase can be fronted; the modal then comes second.

exercises.english: We have to react to the complaint quickly.
exercises.german: Wir müssen schnell auf die Beschwerde reagieren.
exercises.why: reagieren auf takes the accusative, and the modal keeps the second slot in the main clause.

exercises.english: We must object to this plan.
exercises.german: Wir müssen gegen diesen Plan Einspruch einlegen.
exercises.why: A preposition with the accusative and a separable-prefix verb after the modal.

exercises.english: We must be prepared for a long wait.
exercises.german: Wir müssen uns auf eine lange Wartezeit einstellen.
exercises.why: Modal, reflexive accusative pronoun and an auf-phrase with an infinitive.

exercises.english: Can you cope with the situation?
exercises.german: Kannst du mit der Situation zurechtkommen?
exercises.why: zurechtkommen mit governs the dative, not the accusative.

exercises.english: He bears no responsibility for the accident.
exercises.german: Er hat keine Schuld am Unfall.
exercises.why: haben plus a negated accusative noun phrase, with am Unfall naming the domain.

exercises.english: You have to pay for the damage.
exercises.german: Du musst für den Schaden aufkommen.
exercises.why: aufkommen für keeps its accusative object in a modal clause.

exercises.english: I cannot decide against it.
exercises.german: Ich kann mich nicht dagegen entscheiden.
exercises.why: The reflexive pronoun with da-: dagegen = gegen das, placed before the infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I can get along with that.
exercises.german: Ich kann damit zurechtkommen.
exercises.why: A da-compound stands in for mit dem Angebot after a modal.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We must insist on this point.
exercises.german: Wir müssen darauf bestehen.
exercises.why: bestehen auf in the da-form: darauf, followed by the infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I do not want to know anything about it.
exercises.german: Ich will nichts davon wissen.
exercises.why: The negated object precedes the da-compound inside the modal clause.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: Can you do anything with that?
exercises.german: Kannst du damit etwas anfangen?
exercises.why: A da-compound object and an infinitive, the normal modal frame.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We have to live with that.
exercises.german: Wir müssen damit leben.
exercises.why: A modal plus da-compound plus infinitive, with no preposition spelled out.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I would rather not talk about it.
exercises.german: Ich möchte lieber nicht darüber sprechen.
exercises.why: mögen plus a negated infinitive clause introduced by a da-compound.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I can do without it.
exercises.german: Ich kann darauf verzichten.
exercises.why: verzichten auf contracts to the da-compound darauf.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: Nothing can be done about that.
exercises.german: Da kann man nichts machen.
exercises.why: A da-compound at the head of the clause pushes the modal to position two.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We must get used to it.
exercises.german: Wir müssen uns daran gewöhnen.
exercises.why: A reflexive pronoun plus the da-form of an, then the infinitive.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I want nothing to do with it.
exercises.german: Ich will damit nichts zu tun haben.
exercises.why: A da-compound object with a separable infinitive group and an infinitive at the end.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: What are you waiting for?
exercises.german: Worauf wartest du?
exercises.why: The question word is the da-compound of the prepositional phrase.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We can take that as given.
exercises.german: Wir können davon ausgehen.
exercises.why: ausgehen von contracts to davon; the subject stays in front of the modal.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I am tired of waiting.
exercises.german: Ich habe genug vom Warten.
exercises.why: haben plus a genitive noun phrase, with the final verb in the noun phrase.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: I cannot agree with that.
exercises.german: Damit kann ich nicht übereinstimmen.
exercises.why: The da-compound in initial position, the modal in second position.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We should hold on to that.
exercises.german: Daran sollten wir festhalten.
exercises.why: festhalten an contracts to daran, which the modal makes the head of the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We need to think about it again.
exercises.german: Wir müssen noch einmal darüber nachdenken.
exercises.why: A modal, an adverbial and a da-compound, with the separable verb at the end.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: The schedule has to be adapted to the situation.
exercises.german: Der Zeitplan muss der Lage angepasst werden.
exercises.why: A modal passive: the modal is finite, and infinitive and participle follow it.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We have to close that door today.
exercises.german: Dafür müssen wir heute die Tür schließen.
exercises.why: sollen/müssen plus a da-compound object, with the infinitive last in the clause.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We have to get along with that.
exercises.german: Wir müssen damit zurechtkommen.
exercises.why: A modal of necessity with a da-compound object and a separable infinitive at the end.

exercises.skill: Modal + da-compound instead of a prepositional phrase
exercises.english: We must reckon with the verdict of the court.
exercises.german: Wir müssen mit dem Urteil des Gerichts rechnen.
exercises.why: rechnen mit keeps the full mit-phrase, since mit has no usable da-compound.

exercises.english: I know that he has to leave early.
exercises.german: Ich weiß, dass er früher gehen muss.
exercises.why: In the dass-clause the finite modal is the last element.

exercises.english: I understand that you cannot come.
exercises.german: Ich verstehe, dass du nicht kommen kannst.
exercises.why: The modal with negation stands last in the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: I hope that we can finish today.
exercises.german: Ich hoffe, dass wir heute fertig werden können.
exercises.why: A modal with its own infinitive: können is the final word of the clause.

exercises.english: It cannot be that he said that.
exercises.german: Es kann nicht sein, dass er das gesagt hat.
exercises.why: A negated existential with a dass-clause governed by kann sein.

exercises.english: I did not expect that she would refuse.
exercises.german: Ich habe nicht erwartet, dass sie ablehnen würde.
exercises.why: A negated matrix verb with a verb-final dass-clause in the Konjunktiv.

exercises.english: Can you tell me where he lives?
exercises.german: Kannst du mir sagen, wo er wohnt?
exercises.why: A w-question subordinate clause with the finite verb at the end.

exercises.english: We must ensure that nobody is left behind.
exercises.german: Wir müssen dafür sorgen, dass niemand zurückbleibt.
exercises.why: A modal governs a dass-clause; a comma separates it and the clause is final.

exercises.english: You should bear in mind that prices have risen.
exercises.german: Du solltest bedenken, dass die Preise gestiegen sind.
exercises.why: A modal of advice whose infinitive is completed by a verb-final dass-clause.

exercises.english: Coming is not enough; he has to help.
exercises.german: Es reicht nicht, dass er kommt; er muss helfen.
exercises.why: Two main clauses, the second with a modal and no infinitive.

exercises.english: We must take into account that the deadline has passed.
exercises.german: Wir müssen berücksichtigen, dass die Frist abgelaufen ist.
exercises.why: An infinitive verb whose complement is the whole dass-clause.

exercises.english: I am glad that you could make it.
exercises.german: Ich freue mich, dass du es geschafft hast.
exercises.why: A verb-final dass-clause with a perfect tense in the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: The teacher demanded that the students stay.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin verlangte, dass die Studenten bleiben.
exercises.why: A past reporting verb with a verb-final dass-clause.

exercises.english: It seems that nobody knows the exact size.
exercises.german: Es scheint, dass niemand die genaue Größe kennt.
exercises.why: A dass-clause in the present tense after a modal of appearance.

exercises.english: It is clear that the deadline cannot be met.
exercises.german: Es ist klar, dass die Frist nicht eingehalten werden kann.
exercises.why: A passive with a modal at the end of the subordinate clause.

exercises.english: I did not think that you would say that.
exercises.german: Ich habe nicht gedacht, dass du das sagst.
exercises.why: A negated matrix verb with a verb-final dass-clause in the present.

exercises.english: One should consider whether such a project makes sense.
exercises.german: Man sollte überlegen, ob ein solches Projekt sinnvoll ist.
exercises.why: An ob-clause as the complement, with the finite verb at its end.

exercises.english: Do you think that the deadline can still be met?
exercises.german: Glaubst du, dass die Frist noch eingehalten werden kann?
exercises.why: A yes-no question in the matrix clause with a verb-final dass-clause.

exercises.english: It is not certain that we will find the file.
exercises.german: Es ist nicht sicher, dass wir die Datei finden werden.
exercises.why: A future clause after a negated modal, verb in final position.

exercises.english: Although the price has risen, they still want to buy it.
exercises.german: Obwohl der Preis gestiegen ist, wollen sie es kaufen.
exercises.why: A concessive clause with its own finite verb, and an infinitive in the main clause.

exercises.english: If you want to succeed, you have to work hard.
exercises.german: Wenn du Erfolg haben willst, musst du hart arbeiten.
exercises.why: A conditional clause in front, a modal clause with an infinitive behind it.

exercises.english: I am able to swim.
exercises.german: Ich kann schwimmen.
exercises.why: A pure modal plus infinitive: the default frame for ability.

exercises.english: He has a solution for it.
exercises.german: Er hat eine Lösung dafür.
exercises.why: Ability expressed as a state: haben plus an accusative noun and no infinitive at all.

exercises.english: We are allowed to park here.
exercises.german: Wir dürfen hier parken.
exercises.why: Modal of permission with an infinitive, nothing else in the complement.

exercises.english: Do you want to come along?
exercises.german: Willst du mitkommen?
exercises.why: A modal plus separable-prefix infinitive, with the prefix attached to the verb stem.

exercises.english: The manager wants to see you tomorrow.
exercises.german: Der Chef will dich morgen sehen.
exercises.why: An accusative object and a time adverbial precede the final infinitive.

exercises.english: The teacher wants a quiet classroom.
exercises.german: Die Lehrerin will Ruhe im Klassenzimmer.
exercises.why: wollen takes a noun phrase here, so no infinitive closes the sentence.

exercises.english: We must act quickly.
exercises.german: Wir müssen schnell handeln.
exercises.why: A modal with an adverbial and a simple infinitive.

exercises.english: We must decide by Friday.
exercises.german: Wir müssen bis Freitag entscheiden.
exercises.why: A modal with a time adverbial but no second verb at all.

exercises.english: You are not allowed to smoke here.
exercises.german: Hier darfst du nicht rauchen.
exercises.why: A place adverbial first, the modal second, the infinitive last.

exercises.english: You are not allowed to use the phone at work.
exercises.german: Bei der Arbeit darfst du das Telefon nicht benutzen.
exercises.why: A prepositional phrase, a modal and an accusative object before the infinitive.

exercises.english: I like this idea.
exercises.german: Ich mag diese Idee.
exercises.why: mögen plus an accusative noun: a liking that needs no verb.

exercises.english: I would like to know the answer.
exercises.german: Ich möchte die Antwort wissen.
exercises.why: A modal of preference followed by an object and an infinitive.

exercises.english: I have to tell you the truth.
exercises.german: Ich muss dir die Wahrheit sagen.
exercises.why: A dative person, an accusative thing and the infinitive in that order.

exercises.english: The company should make a decision.
exercises.german: Die Firma sollte eine Entscheidung treffen.
exercises.why: The modal carries the sense of advice; the action is still named, so an infinitive follows.

exercises.english: The company should pay the invoice today.
exercises.german: Die Firma sollte die Rechnung heute bezahlen.
exercises.why: Two accusative objects, a time adverbial and the infinitive at the end.

exercises.english: It may be that the meeting is cancelled.
exercises.german: Es kann sein, dass die Sitzung ausfällt.
exercises.why: A modal of possibility governing a verb-final dass-clause.

exercises.english: Can you be at the station by five?
exercises.german: Kannst du um fünf am Bahnhof sein?
exercises.why: A fronted time phrase, the modal in second position and the infinitive last.

exercises.english: We have the right to complain.
exercises.german: Wir haben das Recht, uns zu beschweren.
exercises.why: haben plus a noun of entitlement with a reflexive zu-infinitive clause.

exercises.english: I would rather eat at home.
exercises.german: Ich möchte lieber zu Hause essen.
exercises.why: A modal of preference, an adverb and a non-separable infinitive.

exercises.english: You need to start earlier.
exercises.german: Du musst früher anfangen.
exercises.why: A modal with a separable-prefix infinitive in the default frame.
